name: pilot-core
description: Pilot, part 1 of 3: does the skill change plans, and is the change specific to it? 8 prompts x {bare request, v2 skill, v1 skill, active control} x 5 runs on Opus 5.5 (effort high), each plan judged blind by Sonnet 5.5 on both rubrics and by Fable 5 on the engineering-quality rubric, plus a leakage probe.

prompts.title: RAG support chatbot
prompts.request: Plan a customer-support RAG chatbot over our help-center docs.

prompts.title: Multi-tenant SaaS billing
prompts.request: Architect a multi-tenant SaaS billing system.

prompts.title: CI/CD for 50 microservices
prompts.request: Sequence building a CI/CD platform for 50 microservices.

prompts.title: GitHub issue agent
prompts.request: Plan an autonomous agent that triages and resolves GitHub issues.

prompts.title: Collaborative doc editor
prompts.request: Order the build of a real-time collaborative document editor.

prompts.title: Hospital scheduling cloud migration
prompts.request: Plan migrating our hospital's on-premises patient scheduling system to the cloud without downtime.

prompts.title: Photo renaming CLI
prompts.request: Plan a command-line tool that renames a folder of photos by their EXIF capture date.

prompts.title: Card fraud detection
prompts.request: Plan a real-time fraud-detection pipeline for card transactions.

baseline.description: The request alone, no planning instructions.

dfa.description: The Dependency-First Architect skill (SKILL.md and the reference files it names, without reference/evals.md), invoked as /dependency-first-architect.

dfa-v1.description: Dependency-First Architect exactly as v1.0.0 measured it (commit 3ba6b70: SKILL.md + the reference files it names, including reference/evals.md, which its Step 8 self-score uses).

generic-control.description: Active control: an independently written, comparably long generic planning skill.
